title: Grammar: Comparative Structures — Advanced Use
grammarTip:
Сравнительные структуры в научном письме:

КОЛИЧЕСТВЕННОЕ сравнение:
"significantly / considerably / substantially more/less than"
"twice as much/many as" · "three times higher than"
"slightly / marginally / marginally higher than"

КАЧЕСТВЕННОЕ сравнение:
"similar to / comparable to / analogous to"
"in contrast to / unlike / as opposed to"
"whereas / while / on the other hand"

САМОЕ ВАЖНОЕ (superlative in academic):
"the most significant finding was..."
"the least effective method proved to be..."

💡 Избегай "more better" и "most biggest" — double comparative/superlative!
✅ "more effective" · "the most effective" (не "the most more effective")

grammarTable.subject: Standard comparative
grammarTable.example: "Larger studies are more reliable than small ones." / "This method is faster than the previous one."

grammarTable.subject: Amplified comparative
grammarTable.example: "The new treatment was considerably more effective." / "Far fewer side effects were observed."

grammarTable.subject: Near-equality
grammarTable.verb: almost/nearly as + adj + as / not quite as + adj + as
grammarTable.example: "The results were nearly as significant as expected." / "It is not quite as straightforward as it appears."

grammarTable.subject: Proportional: the...the
grammarTable.short: as one increases, so does the other
grammarTable.example: "The larger the sample, the more reliable the results." / "The more data we have, the clearer the picture becomes."

grammarTable.subject: Double comparative
grammarTable.example: "Science is becoming more and more open." / "The data became less and less consistent as time went on."

grammarTable.subject: Comparative with the
grammarTable.example: "Of the two methods, the first is the more reliable." / "Which is the better approach?"

rows.form: Far / much / considerably / significantly + comparative
rows.example: "The new approach is far more efficient." / "Results were significantly better than the control."

rows.form: Slightly / a little / somewhat + comparative
rows.example: "The effect was slightly larger in the second trial." / "Somewhat more promising results were observed."

rows.form: Roughly / approximately twice/three times as + adj + as
rows.example: "The new drug is approximately twice as effective as the existing one."

rows.form: No + comparative (= not any more than)
rows.example: "The new method is no more accurate than the original." (= they are equal in accuracy)

grammarExtra.title: The More... The More: Proportional Structures

rows.form: The + comparative clause, the + comparative clause
rows.example: "The more carefully the experiment is designed, the more reliable the results will be."

rows.form: Can use adjectives, adverbs, or nouns
rows.example: "The greater the sample size, the smaller the margin of error." / "The earlier we act, the less damage will occur."

rows.form: Can express inverse proportionality
rows.example: "The more exposure the subject has, the less effective the treatment becomes."

rows.form: Both clauses often use the same tense
rows.example: "The more scientists share data, the faster progress is made."

grammarExtra.title: As...As and Not As...As: Equality and Near-Equality

rows.form: As + adj/adv + as = equal degree
rows.example: "The placebo performed as well as the active drug in this trial."

rows.form: Not as + adj + as = lower degree
rows.example: "The second treatment was not as effective as the first."

rows.form: Nearly/almost/just as + adj + as = very close to equal
rows.example: "The generic drug is nearly as effective as the brand version."

rows.form: Twice / half / three times as + adj + as = proportional
rows.example: "The new compound is three times as potent as the original molecule."

grammarExtra.title: Comparatives in Scientific Writing: Useful Patterns

rows.form: Comparing results: significantly/considerably + comparative
rows.example: "Group A showed significantly higher cognitive performance than Group B."

rows.form: Expressing trends: more and more / increasingly + comparative
rows.example: "Pre-registration is becoming more and more common in clinical research."

rows.form: Discussing proportions: the more X, the more Y
rows.example: "The more stringent the methodology, the greater the confidence in the results."

rows.form: Comparing methods: not as... as / far more... than
rows.example: "Traditional peer review is not as effective as post-publication review at catching errors."

rows.form: ❌ The results were more better than expected.
rows.example: ✅ The results were better than expected. (no "more" with -er comparatives)

rows.form: ❌ The larger is the sample, the reliable are the results.
rows.example: ✅ The larger the sample, the more reliable the results. ("the + comparative", no verb needed)

rows.form: ❌ She works more harder than her colleague.
rows.example: ✅ She works harder than her colleague. (no "more" with -er adverbs)

rows.form: ❌ This is the most effective of the two methods.
rows.example: ✅ This is the more effective of the two methods. ("most" for 3+; "more" for exactly two)

exercises.text: "The results were ___ more significant than the preliminary data had suggested."
"The ___ the sample size, the ___ accurate the estimates will be." (both increase)
exercises.hint: "The + comparative, the + comparative" = both comparatives needed

exercises.text: "The generic drug is ___ effective as the branded version."
exercises.hint: "Nearly as + adjective + as" = almost equal but slightly less

exercises.text: "Group A performed ___ ___ than Group B across all measures." (significantly / well)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct structure for two options.
exercises.text: "Of the two analytical methods, the second is ___ reliable."
exercises.hint: "The + comparative" = choosing between exactly two options

exercises.text: "The new compound is approximately three times ___ potent ___ the original molecule."
exercises.hint: "X times as + adjective + as" = proportional equality

exercises.text: "___ stringent the methodology, ___ the confidence in the results."
exercises.hint: "The + comparative, the + comparative" = full proportional structure

exercises.text: "Research data is becoming ___ and ___ openly available as journals change their policies."

opts: The results were more better than expected.
The results were considerably better than expected.
The results were most better than expected.
The results were much more better than expected.
exercises.correct: The results were considerably better than expected.

exercises.text: "The ___ the confounding variables are controlled, the ___ meaningful the results become."
exercises.hint: "The more X, the more Y" — both comparatives, even if expressing quality increase

exercises.text: "The new vaccine is ___ as effective as existing vaccines."
exercises.hint: "Not quite as + adjective + as" = slightly below equal

exercises.text: "The treatment group performed ___ ___ than the control group did." (far / well)
"This is ___ of the two approaches: it requires less data collection but produces comparable results."
exercises.hint: "The + comparative" = choosing between exactly two options

exercises.text: "The peer-reviewed version is ___ accurate than the preprint." (= equally accurate)
exercises.hint: "No more + comparative + than" = no greater than, equal to

opts: the better the picture we get.
exercises.correct: the better the picture we get.
exercises.hint: "The more X, the better Y" — second clause: "the + comparative + subject + verb"

exercises.instruction: Choose the most appropriate for scientific writing.
exercises.text: "The experimental group showed ___ improvement than the control group."

questions.text: "The new methodology was ___ more efficient than the previous one." (very strong difference)
"The ___ carefully variables are controlled, the ___ confident researchers can be." (proportional)
"The treatment group performed ___ the control group did." (not equal — slightly less)
"Of the two designs, the second is ___ robust." (choosing between exactly two)
"The new drug is approximately twice ___ effective ___ the existing treatment."
questions.hint: "X times as + adjective + as" = proportional equality

questions.text: "The results were more better than expected" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: No "more" with -er comparatives: "better than" not "more better"

questions.text: "Pre-registration is becoming ___ and ___ common across scientific disciplines." (progressive increase)
"The ___ independent studies confirm a finding, the ___ established it becomes."
questions.hint: "The more X, the more Y" = proportional structure

questions.text: "The experimental treatment was ___ ___ than the standard therapy in all measured outcomes." (significantly / good)
"The open data version was ___ as comprehensive as the original dataset." (almost equal)
questions.hint: "Nearly as + adjective + as" = very close to equal

questions.text: "The ___ the exposure, the ___ the immune response." (both increase together)
questions.hint: "The greater X, the stronger Y" = proportional comparative

questions.text: Which sentence uses a comparative correctly in formal scientific writing?
opts: Results were much more better in Group A.
Group A did considerably better than Group B.
The results was significantly most better.
Group A performed the most better of the two.
questions.correct: Group A did considerably better than Group B.
